import subprocess
def atlas(rows):
    lines = [f'ATLAS {len(rows)}'] + rows
    p = subprocess.run(['/workspace/tmp/engine'], input=('\n'.join(lines)+'\n').encode(),
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    return p.stdout.decode().splitlines(), p.returncode

# n=0 -> one full-domain null run

# /0 route only
print(atlas(['00000000000000000000000000000000 0 5']))
# /0 + /128 + wrap-around /1 (start 0x8000..0 covers to U)
print(atlas(['00000000000000000000000000000000 0 5',
             '00000000000000000000000000000000 128 9',
             '80000000000000000000000000000000 1 7',
             'ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff 128 3']))
# overlapping LPM
print(atlas(['00000000000000000000000000000000 0 1',
             '00000000000000000000000000000000 4 2',
             '00000000000000000000000000000000 8 3']))
# hop 0 real vs null: two same-hop adjacent -> coalesce
print(atlas(['00000000000000000000000000000000 1 0',
             '80000000000000000000000000000000 1 0']))
